primitives.name: Sequential Stimulus Compound Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: THE PATTERNING OF STIMULUS COMPOUNDS 369 pounds, but with this difference: the high-pitched buzzer was sounded for one second; then, after a pause of one second, the low-pitched buzzer was sounded for one second, following which the shutter was raised, giving the dog access to the bar.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: t_1, t_2: duration of stimuli (s); \Delta\tau: inter-stimulus interval (s); S_H, S_L: sensory input vectors (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Stimuli are perfectly localized in time; the agent possesses a working memory buffer capable of bridging the inter-stimulus interval \Delta\tau.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when \Delta\tau exceeds the biological or computational decay constant of the short-term memory trace, collapsing the compound into independent, uncorrelated events.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a time-shifted convolution operator in GSE, mapping distinct temporal features into a unified situational state vector.
layer2.telemetry: Latency and accuracy of response immediately following the completion of the second stimulus.

primitives.name: Differential Reinforcement Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: After each of these presentations the shutter was lifted, but if the dog nosed the bar no food would be given.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: R: Reward scalar (Joules or dimensionless utility); A: Action indicator variable (0 or 1); C: Contextual state vector
primitives.assumptions: Reward function is strictly deterministic based on the contextual state; omission of reward provides a symmetric negative gradient signal.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities emerge under stochastic reward schedules or when the baseline probability of spontaneous action approaches zero, halting gradient descent.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to the GSI loss function, applying a penalty term to policy gradients when actions are executed in unreinforced contexts.
layer2.telemetry: Rate of action suppression (percentage decrease in bar-nosing) across successive unreinforced trials.

primitives.name: Ogival Convergence Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: There is the same initial depression of all three curves at the outset of differential reinforcement, and the same subsequent rise of all three to 100 per cent; following this the two non-reinforced component combinations gradually fall toward zero, taking a roughly ogival course.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P(t): Probability of correct discrimination (dimensionless, [0,1]); n: Trial count (dimensionless); \sigma: Learning rate variance
primitives.assumptions: Learning dynamics follow a sigmoidal accumulation of evidence; initial exploration causes uniform response elevation before differentiation occurs.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Convergence stalls if the similarity metric between reinforced and unreinforced compounds exceeds the discriminator's resolution threshold.

layer2.mapping: Represents the GSI conformal calibration curve, tracking the decay of non-conformity scores for false-positive state predictions over time.
layer2.telemetry: Area under the learning curve (AUC) and the trial index at which asymptotic performance is reached.

reasoning_traces.think:
The experimental paradigm establishes a rigorous framework for analyzing how sequential information is integrated into actionable state representations. By presenting distinct auditory stimuli (high and low buzzers) separated by a precise temporal gap, the system forces the subject to maintain a transient memory state. This process can be mathematically formalized as a non-commutative operation: the sequence (H,L) yields a fundamentally different internal state than (L,H) or the repeated sequences (H,H) and (L,L). The core mechanism driving learning is the differential reinforcement kernel. When the specific temporal compound (H,L) is presented, an action (nosing the bar) results in a positive reward scalar. Conversely, identical actions following the negative compounds result in reward omission. This asymmetry creates a steep gradient in the policy space, compelling the agent to refine its internal discriminator.

The observed 'ogival course' of the learning curves provides critical insight into the underlying optimization dynamics. Initially, all stimulus presentations elicit a generalized exploratory response, leading to a uniform elevation in action probability. As the differential reinforcement continues, the agent begins to isolate the unique features of the reinforced sequence. The error rates for the negative compounds subsequently decay toward zero, mirroring the tightening of confidence intervals in a Bayesian inference model. This mathematical duality highlights that behavioral patterning is not merely rote memorization, but a continuous process of hypothesis testing and probabilistic updating. The failure modes of this system are equally instructive; if the inter-stimulus interval exceeds the decay time of the sensory trace, the compound collapses, and the non-commutative structure dissolves into independent events, rendering the task unsolvable.
